identificationModule.officialTitle: Clinical Study of the Safety and Efficacy of Next-generation Universal CD19 Chimeric Antigen Receptor T Cells in the Treatment of Relapsed or Refractory B Cell Malignancies

descriptionModule.detailedDescription: CD19-UCART is a kind of "off-the-shelf" product originated from health donor's PBMC. This is an open-label, single arm study to evaluate the safety and anti- tumor efficacy of Next-generation CD19-UCART in the treatment of relapsed or refractory B-cell hematological malignancies.

primaryOutcomes.description: Incidence of adverse events (AEs) defined as DLTs
primaryOutcomes.timeFrame: Day 0 up to 35 days after T cell infusion

secondaryOutcomes.description: Proportion of patients in whom a response among complete response and partial response as defined by standard disease-specific criteria, will be observed.

otherOutcomes.description: DOR is defined as the time from the first objective response to disease progression or death due to disease relapse or drug-related toxicity
otherOutcomes.timeFrame: up to 2 years after T cell infusion

otherOutcomes.description: PFS is defined as the time from the T cell infusion date to the date of disease progression or death from any cause
otherOutcomes.timeFrame: up to 2 years after T cell infusion

otherOutcomes.description: OS is defined as the time from the date of leukapheresis until death from any cause
otherOutcomes.timeFrame: up to 2 years after T cell infusion
